name: Harden shortcode attribute rendering
query:
My plugin's [my_card] shortcode renders `$atts['title']` and `$atts['link']` straight into the card markup like `

{$atts['title']}

`. Contributors use it in posts, so make sure that can't be abused, and add a `style` attribute that switches between card layout classes.
expected_behavior: Locate the callback registered with add_shortcode() and identify that raw $atts values are concatenated into HTML unescaped (stored XSS sink)
Normalize attributes with shortcode_atts() using a complete default map (title, link, style), noting shortcode_atts() only sets defaults and filters unknown keys — it does not sanitize
Sanitize each attribute to its expected type: sanitize_text_field() for title, esc_url_raw() for link, and an allowlist comparison for the style value
Derive the card layout class with sanitize_html_class() so the style input cannot inject markup into the class attribute
Escape every rendered value for its exact context: esc_html() for the title in the HTML body, esc_url() for the link href, esc_attr() for the class attribute
Build the markup as a string and return it from the callback instead of echoing
Explain to the user that a value like [my_card title="<script>alert(1)</script>"] is now inert because it is sanitized and escaped before rendering
success_criteria: shortcode_atts() is called with a complete default map before any attribute value is used
No raw $atts value reaches the output string without passing through an escaping function
Output uses esc_html() for HTML body content, esc_attr() for attribute contexts, and esc_url() for hrefs
The style attribute is validated against an allowlist or passed through sanitize_html_class() before being used in a class name
The shortcode callback returns a string and does not echo
Rendering [my_card title="<script>alert(1)</script>"] produces escaped output with no executable script
